summary: A real-time deduction puzzle where all players simultaneously race to find the shortest path to move a target robot to its goal, with robots sliding until they hit a wall or another robot. It's less a game and more a shared puzzle-solving competition, prized for how it sharpens spatial reasoning under time pressure.
praised: Great for mixed-skill and mixed-age groups
criticised: Real-time format can intimidate slower thinkers
Not really a 'game' in the traditional sense—no hidden info or strategy across turns
Can be dominated by a few fast players

interaction.kind: shared puzzle board, robots block each other
interaction.detail: All robots sit on one shared board and every player is solving the same puzzle simultaneously in real time. The core mechanic is that a moving robot only stops when it hits a wall or another player's robot, so opponents' pieces directly shape what routes are possible.

scoring.how_you_win: Players race in real time to call out the fewest moves needed to route the matching robot to its target; whoever proves a valid solution at that count claims the chip, and whoever holds the most chips when the target deck runs out wins.
